implementation_state: The upstream contracts this node was blocked on are closed: ACCOUNT, NEWAPI, I2, I3 and I4 all pass their gates, so the blocked_by set is emptied and the node is no longer waiting on upstream. Its own gates are still unmet, but the reason has changed and the previous text is now false. There is one backend lifecycle with a production caller: the check-in runtime owns a headed browser session per (provider, account), and a WAF challenge holds that session rather than destroying it, so a resume continues the same session and never asks the operator to authenticate twice. There is one real product surface driving it: four Tauri commands and a per-account maintenance row with start, resume, cancel and a written record of what was observed rather than what was hoped for. Migration and takeover rollback surfaces still do not exist, and a check-in confirmation is not a rollback confirmation — one interrupts a human and resumes, the other has to undo a half-applied change, and only the first is built. The surface has never been click-tested in a running application: it compiles, it is unit-tested, and no person has watched it work end to end. The other core engines remain fixtures rather than surfaces a user can drive. See E-131 and E-132.
